source.title: Emergent Generalization by Representation Learning in Artificial Neural Networks
source.authors: Hardik Rajpal; Dan F. M. Goodman

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses grokking and reports its own results on representation emergence and generalisation, but it does not test any listed version's defining delayed-accuracy pattern or mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior grokking results and describes its own non-monotonic emergence measure as coinciding with a grokking transition. It does not report training and test accuracy evolving from saturation/chance to a delayed test-accuracy jump. Its time-series prediction and bottleneck results are recorded below as related findings, not as tests of a listed version. The mouse analysis is excluded because it is biological neural data, not an AI model result.
record.test_reason: The authors call their memorisation-to-generalisation phase a grokking transition, but never show it. They report no train/test curves with delayed generalisation; the abstract says prediction loss falls monotonically. The setup is a reservoir network with a bottleneck on chaotic time-series prediction, trained for 100 epochs with Adam. The tracked quantity is an information-theoretic emergence measure (Ψ), not delayed test performance. No version's defining pattern or mechanism is measured, so this is a related construct, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a bottleneck forcing low-dimensional representations is necessary for rotational and OOD generalisation in their task. They find emergence (Ψ) follows a non-monotonic trajectory that scales with task complexity and predicts generalisation, and they assert this coincides with the grokking transition. Mouse CA1/PFC data show analogous non-monotonic emergence. They note it is unclear whether emergence is necessary for generalisation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a modified reservoir network trained for time-series prediction, a trainable bottleneck, and information-theoretic measures; it does not reproduce the original small-algorithmic-dataset grokking setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Bottleneck presence affects generalisation; bottleneck size and task complexity are varied. The paper reports that prediction loss changes with task complexity and bottleneck size.

fits_no_version.finding: A bottleneck reservoir network generalises to unseen rotations and held-out attractors. Without the bottleneck, it fits training data but fails to generalise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An explicit low-dimensional bottleneck enables rotation-invariant OOD generalisation in reservoir time-series prediction.

fits_no_version.finding: Ψ first decreases, then rises during training while MSE falls monotonically. Ψ's final level is higher for more complex tasks, and its transition precedes the information-bottleneck transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Causal emergence of learned latents is non-monotonic during training even when loss decreases monotonically.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalised macro predictability is negatively associated with prediction loss. Micro predictability is positively associated with loss once macro predictability is conditioned on.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Predictive yet distributed latent representations accompany lower OOD prediction loss.

record.problems: The paper does not report the delayed train/test accuracy pattern in the claim. The main AI generalisation comparisons are described qualitatively in the text; numerical values are not stated there. The information measures assume multivariate Gaussian states and capture only linear dependencies. The authors state that it is unclear whether causal emergence is necessary for generalisation.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant AI-model result rows were left out. The mouse neural-data analysis and cited results from other studies are not recorded as AI-model rows.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets and no delayed test-accuracy jump after training saturation. The dependence of the delay on training-set size is also untested.
No generalising circuit is identified and no removal of memorising components is tracked. Ψ is not shown to anticipate a test-performance jump, because no such jump is reported.
The data are non-algorithmic time series, but no grokking-like delay in test loss is reported. Initialization scale and weight norm are not manipulated.
No weight decay or norm analysis, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms learned across runs.
Optimizer and numerical artifacts are not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The grokking link rests on citation and interpretation (refs 29 and 39), not on a measured delayed-generalisation curve. Loss is reported as monotonically decreasing, which, if anything, argues against a grokking-like delay here. It is not counted as a challenge because test-loss trajectories over epochs are not separately reported. The mouse analysis is biological data and correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not use small algorithmic datasets or report training and test accuracy showing a delayed jump.

It measures a non-monotonic causal-emergence quantity, but does not identify an algorithmic generalising circuit, track removal of memorising components, or show a progress measure anticipating a test-accuracy jump.
The study does not test grokking-like delays on images, text, or molecules, or manipulate initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The study does not test weight decay, low-norm efficiency, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test optimizer or numerical artifacts as an explanation of grokking.

rows.subject: modified reservoir computing network with a bottleneck layer
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the Ψ causal-emergence measure across training epochs

conditions.value: Ψ normalised by its absolute value at the first epoch

rows.baseline: first training epoch used for normalisation
rows.value: The measure initially decreases, reaches a minimum, and then increases to a maximum during the generalisation phase.
rows.locator: Results, Learned Latent Representations are Causally Emergent; Figure 4B-C description
rows.note: The authors describe this trajectory as coinciding with the grokking phenomenon; no test-accuracy jump is reported.
rows.check: The Ψ trajectory is observed, but the link to grokking is the authors' assertion. Fig. 4B reports MSE decreasing monotonically, so no delayed generalisation jump is shown. This should not be read as evidence for V1, V2 or V3.
